narrative.title: The Escalator Inspector's Left Slide
narrative.scenario: A mall maintenance bot inspects a tree of escalators without any recursive subroutines — its firmware only allows a loop and a work-pile. Its trick: slide leftward as far as possible, parking every landing on the pile, then service the top landing, and re-emerge on its right branch to repeat. Landings get stamped exactly between their two descents, matching the official left-self-right sweep sheet.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array of node values in inorder, produced without recursion.
constraints: No recursive calls allowed — the traversal must run on an explicit stack

testCases.explanation: Left wing bottoms out at 4, unwinds 4,2,5, then the root, then 3,6.
The single node is parked, popped, and recorded in one pass.

hintLevels: Level 1: Inorder needs each node held back until its left subtree is finished — a stack can park it there.
Level 2: Keep one running pointer: push while sliding left, then pop-and-record, then jump to the popped node's right subtree.
Level 3: The two loop conditions (pointer alive OR stack non-empty) together form the driver; each node is pushed and popped exactly once.
